title: The novel TAK1 inhibitor handelin inhibits NF-kappaB and AP-1 activity to alleviate elastase-induced emphysema in mice.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然产物handelin抑制TAK1激酶以缓解肺气肿，涉及NF-kB/AP-1炎症通路，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: AIMS: Emphysema, one of the two major components of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), is driven by aberrant inflammatory responses and associated with irreversible lung parenchymal destruction. As effective therapy for preventing or treating COPD/emphysema is yet unavailable, development of molecular targets and therapeutic agents for COPD/emphysema is required. MAIN METHODS AND KEY FINDINGS: We identified handelin-a guaianolide dimer of sesquiterpene lactones- from a chemical library of 431 natural products as it exhibited potent inhibitory effects on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced nitric oxide (NO) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, LPS-induced activation of nuclear factor kappaB (NF-kappaB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)/AP-1, and expression of proinflammatory mediators in macrophage cells. In silico docking and biochemical studies enabled the identification of the ATP-binding pocket of transforming growth factor beta-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), a kinase upstream of NF-kappaB and MAPK/AP-1 pathways, as a molecular target for handelin. Moreover, oral administration of handelin (10 mg/kg) suppressed elastase-induced development of emphysematous phenotypes, including lung function disturbance, airspace enlargement, and increases in the level of neutrophils and CD8+ T cells in lung tissues, without overt toxicity. Consistent with in vitro results, analyses of lung tissues revealed that treatment with handelin suppressed elastase-induced NF-kappaB and AP-1 activation in the lungs, followed by downregulation of their targets including interleukin-6 (IL-6), inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), and matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9). SIGNIFICANCE: These findings suggest that handelin, as a TAK1 inhibitor, effectively prevents development of emphysema in an elastase-induced mouse model by inhibiting a proinflammatory mediators mediated by NF-kappaB and AP-1.
abstract_zh: 目的：肺气肿是慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）的两大主要组成部分之一，由异常炎症反应驱动，并与不可逆的肺实质破坏相关。由于目前尚无有效疗法可预防或治疗COPD/肺气肿，因此亟需开发针对COPD/肺气肿的分子靶点和治疗药物。主要方法和关键发现：我们从431种天然产物的化学库中鉴定出汉德林（handelin）——一种愈创木烷型倍半萜内酯二聚体——因其对脂多糖（LPS）诱导的一氧化氮（NO）和活性氧（ROS）产生、LPS诱导的核因子κB（NF-κB）和丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）/AP-1的激活，以及巨噬细胞中促炎介质的表达表现出强效抑制作用。通过计算机模拟对接和生化研究，我们确定了转化生长因子β激活激酶1（TAK1）的ATP结合口袋——NF-κB和MAPK/AP-1通路上游的一种激酶——作为汉德林的分子靶点。此外，口服汉德林（10 mg/kg）抑制了弹性蛋白酶诱导的肺气肿表型发展，包括肺功能紊乱、气腔扩大以及肺组织中中性粒细胞和CD8+ T细胞水平的升高，且无明显毒性。与体外结果一致，肺组织分析显示，汉德林处理抑制了肺中弹性蛋白酶诱导的NF-κB和AP-1激活，随后下调了其靶标，包括白细胞介素-6（IL-6）、诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）和基质金属蛋白酶9（MMP9）。意义：这些发现表明，汉德林作为TAK1抑制剂，通过抑制由NF-κB和AP-1介导的促炎介质，有效预防了弹性蛋白酶诱导的小鼠模型中肺气肿的发展。
